name: United Kingdom
tagline: Still the best-known route out of the IB, and now one of the most expensive
summary: The UK runs one central application system, UCAS, for almost every undergraduate course in the country. You pick five courses, write one personal statement for all of them, and universities make conditional offers in IB points, usually something like '36 points overall including HL 6,6,5'. Since Brexit you are treated as an international student: you pay overseas tuition, you need a Student visa, and you cannot borrow from the UK student loan system. The teaching and the offer system are excellent; the money is the problem.
whyConsider: One application covers up to five courses across the whole country
Offers are made in IB points and HL grades, so you know exactly what you are aiming for
Everything is taught in English, and degrees in England and Wales take three years, like Denmark’s
Very deep subject specialisation from day one, and strong course-level reputations far beyond Oxbridge
Scotland's four-year degrees let you keep two or three subjects open before you specialise
watchOuts: You pay international tuition. At Glasgow that is GBP 28,275-38,670 for 2027/28, and medicine is far higher
No access to UK tuition fee loans or maintenance loans as an EU citizen; you must fund it yourself
The Graduate Route post-study work visa is 18 months, not 2 years, for applications made on or after 1 January 2027 - so 18 months by the time you graduate
The 15 October deadline for Oxford, Cambridge, medicine, dentistry and veterinary is a full three months before everyone else
Admissions tests (UCAT, LNAT, ESAT, TMUA, TARA) have registration deadlines in September, before the UCAS deadline itself

ibRecognition.minimumPoints: No national minimum. Offers are set course by course; the competitive research universities typically ask 34-39 points overall.
ibRecognition.subjectLevelRule: Offers are expressed as a total plus three Higher Level grades. The University of Glasgow states its Economics requirement as '36 (6,6,5)' plus 'HL English or Humanities and HL Mathematics (Analysis & Approaches)'. LSE publishes a range of '37 points overall (with three Higher level subjects at grades 6 6 6) to 39 points overall (with three Higher level subjects at grades 7 6 6)'. Named HL subjects are common, and quantitative courses increasingly require HL Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches specifically.
ibRecognition.gradeConversion: The UCAS Tariff scores each IB component separately; there is no single Tariff figure for the Diploma as a whole. IBO Certificate in Higher Level: H7 = 56, H6 = 48, H5 = 32, H4 = 24, H3 = 12, H2 and H1 = 0. IBO Certificate in Standard Level: S7 = 28, S6 = 24, S5 = 16, S4 = 12, S3 = 6, S2 and S1 = 0. IBO Certificate in Extended Essay and IBO Certificate in Theory of Knowledge each: A = 12, B = 10, C = 8, D = 6, E = 4. CAS carries no Tariff points because it is not accredited.
notes: Most selective universities ignore the Tariff for IB applicants and make offers directly in points and HL grades. The Tariff matters mainly for less selective courses and for Clearing.

UCAS states the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge certificates were accredited in their own right and are awarded Tariff points 'when the certificates have been taken individually' - check with the university how your core points are counted inside a full Diploma.
LSE warns that 'offers made may also change from year to year' depending on the strength of the applicant pool, so published requirements are guidelines, not guarantees.
The IB Diploma itself requires 24 points or more to be awarded; UCAS records this but attaches no Tariff points to the Diploma as a whole.

deadlines.label: UCAS applications open for 2027 entry
deadlines.notes: You can start filling in the application from this date.

deadlines.label: UCAT (medicine and dentistry) - account registration, bursary and access arrangements open
deadlines.notes: Published on UCAT's test dates page as "20 May 2026 (14:00 UK Time)". You create the account first; test booking opens a month later.

deadlines.label: UCAT (medicine and dentistry) - booking opens
deadlines.notes: Published on UCAT's test dates page as "23 June 2026 (14:00 UK Time)". The 2026 cycle is the one that feeds 2027 entry — UCAT's own home page says registration instructions for UCAT 2027 will be published later, and that cycle belongs to 2028 entry. Booking deadline and testing window are separate entries.

deadlines.label: UCAT (medicine and dentistry) - testing window
deadlines.notes: Published on UCAT's test dates page as a window beginning "13 July 2026" and ending "24 September 2026", which the page labels the "Last test day". Your sitting must fall inside this window, and the window closes eight days after the booking deadline, so a late booking leaves almost no choice of slot. Context, not a milestone: UCAT publishes results to universities in "Early November" with no day given — you get your own score on the day you test.

deadlines.label: UAT-UK admissions tests (ESAT, TMUA, TARA) - test booking for the October sitting
deadlines.notes: Published as "Test booking opens for October 2026" on 20 July 2026 3pm BST, closing 28 September 2026 6pm BST. The time is the closing time. Accounts for 2027 entry opened on 1 June 2026. Oxford and Cambridge applicants must use this October sitting apart from a few exceptions.

deadlines.label: LNAT (law) - registration opens
deadlines.year: 2026/27 LNAT cycle, used for September 2027 entry
deadlines.notes: Published as "LNAT registration begins" on 1 August 2026. You cannot book a slot before this. Oxford and Cambridge applicants have only six weeks from here to register and book.

deadlines.label: First date completed applications can be submitted
deadlines.notes: Nothing is sent to universities before this date.

deadlines.label: LNAT (law) - testing begins
deadlines.year: 2026/27 LNAT cycle, used for September 2027 entry
deadlines.notes: Published as "LNAT testing begins" on 1 September 2026. The first day a booked slot can actually be sat; the sitting deadlines that follow differ by university.

deadlines.label: LNAT (law) - register and book, Oxford and Cambridge
deadlines.notes: Published as "Register and book by 15 September 2026". Registration opening and the start of testing are separate entries.

deadlines.label: UCAT (medicine and dentistry) - booking deadline
deadlines.notes: Published on UCAT's test dates page as "16 September 2026 (15:00 UK Time)". Miss it and you cannot apply to UCAT medical schools this cycle; UCAT's home page states the consortium makes no exceptions. The last day you can actually sit the test is 24 September 2026, which is its own entry.

deadlines.label: UAT-UK admissions tests (ESAT, TMUA, TARA) - October sitting
deadlines.notes: Published as "tests 12-16 October 2026". Oxford and Cambridge applicants must use this October sitting apart from a few exceptions.

deadlines.label: Oxford, Cambridge, medicine, dentistry and veterinary medicine/science
deadlines.notes: UCAS’s deadline for these courses, three months before everyone else’s. UCAS says it is unusual for these universities to consider a late application, so treat 18:00 UK time on 15 October as the end. Admissions test registration closes even earlier.

deadlines.label: LNAT (law) - sit the test, Oxford and Cambridge
deadlines.notes: Published as "sit by 15 October 2026". Registration and booking close a month earlier, on 15 September 2026.

deadlines.label: UAT-UK admissions tests (ESAT, TMUA, TARA) - test booking for the January sitting
deadlines.notes: Published as test booking from 26 October 2026 3pm GMT to 21 December 2026 6pm GMT (registration reopens 5 October 2026). The time is the closing time. Not available for Oxford or Cambridge applicants. Other universities let you pick a sitting.

deadlines.label: LNAT (law) - sit the test, KCL, LSE and UCL
deadlines.notes: Published as "KCL, LSE and UCL: sit by 31 December 2026". LNAT universities listed are Cambridge, Oxford, King's College London, LSE, UCL, Bristol, Durham and SUSS (Singapore).

deadlines.label: UAT-UK admissions tests (ESAT, TMUA, TARA) - January sitting
deadlines.notes: Published as "tests 4-8 January 2027". Not available for Oxford or Cambridge applicants.

deadlines.label: Main equal consideration deadline (all other courses)
deadlines.notes: Every application that arrives by this time must be given equal consideration. Applications after it are only looked at if places remain.

deadlines.label: LNAT (law) - register, book and sit, Bristol and Durham
deadlines.notes: Published as "Bristol and Durham: register, book and sit by 13 January 2027". LNAT universities listed are Cambridge, Oxford, King's College London, LSE, UCL, Bristol, Durham and SUSS (Singapore).

deadlines.label: LNAT (law) - register, all other universities
deadlines.notes: Published as "All others: register by 20 January 2027". LNAT universities listed are Cambridge, Oxford, King's College London, LSE, UCL, Bristol, Durham and SUSS (Singapore).

deadlines.label: LNAT (law) - sit the test, all other universities
deadlines.notes: Published as "All others: ... sit by 25 January 2027". Registration for these universities closes on 20 January 2027. LNAT universities listed are Cambridge, Oxford, King's College London, LSE, UCL, Bristol, Durham and SUSS (Singapore).

deadlines.label: Extra opens
deadlines.notes: For applicants holding no offers.

deadlines.label: Final date for applications to be sent to universities
deadlines.notes: UCAS: "Applications received by this deadline will be sent to universities and colleges." Apply after it and your application goes into Clearing, where you can only apply for courses that still have places. The last day to apply at all is 23 September 2027.

deadlines.label: Clearing opens
deadlines.notes: IB results come out 6 July, so Clearing is already open when you get them.

deadlines.label: LNAT (law) - late applications from international applicants: book your test
deadlines.notes: The LNAT dates page runs a separate late route for international applicants who send the UCAS form by 30 June 2027: book the test slot by 25 July 2027 and sit it by 31 July 2027. As an international applicant this is the only LNAT window still open after the January deadlines have passed, so it is worth knowing it exists — but it depends on the law course still having places.

deadlines.label: LNAT (law) - late applications from international applicants: sit the test
deadlines.notes: The last sitting date on the whole LNAT calendar for this cycle. Booking for it closes on 25 July 2027, which is its own entry.

deadlines.label: Final application deadline for 2027 entry
deadlines.notes: Last date to apply at all for autumn 2027.

steps: From May 2026 you create one UCAS account and fill in one application. You choose up to five courses; for medicine, dentistry and veterinary you may only choose four in that subject.
You write a personal statement. From 2026 entry UCAS changed it from one long essay to three separate questions, and the same statement goes to all five courses.
A teacher at your school writes one academic reference. Ask early - references take time.
Register separately for any admissions test your course needs (UCAT, LNAT, ESAT, TMUA or TARA). These registrations close in September, before the UCAS deadline.
Submit by 15 October 2026 if you are applying to Oxford, Cambridge, medicine, dentistry or veterinary; otherwise by 13 January 2027.
Universities reply with conditional offers stated in IB points and HL grades. Some courses interview between December and March.
You reply with one firm choice and one insurance choice, then your IB results in July are matched against the conditions automatically.
application.selectionNotes: Every course is selective and sets its own conditions - there is no open access. Selection is on predicted grades, the personal statement, the reference, and for some courses an admissions test and interview. Oxford and Cambridge interview most shortlisted applicants in December. The UCAS application fee for the 2027 cycle is GBP 34.50 for up to five choices (it was GBP 28.95 for 2026 entry).

language.englishTaughtBachelors: Everything. All undergraduate teaching is in English.
language.englishProof: UK universities generally accept IB English A at a specified grade, and often IB English B HL, as proof of English. Exact accepted grades vary by university; check each course page. A Student visa also requires English at the level set out in the immigration rules, which your university confirms on your CAS.
notes: Scottish universities teach in English too; Gaelic is not needed.
Because requirements are set per university, confirm the exact IB English grade accepted on the course page rather than assuming.

tuitionEuEea.value: Most EU students pay the international rate. In England, settled or pre-settled status, or (for autumn 2027, the last intake) being Irish or a UK national long resident in the EEA, can mean Home fees. Scotland sets its own rules.

tuitionNonEu.value: University of Glasgow 2027/28: Arts and Social Sciences GBP 28,275; Science, Engineering, Nursing and Medical/Veterinary/Life Sciences GBP 33,708; Veterinary Medicine and Surgery GBP 38,670 (Medicine MBChB and Dentistry BDS listed as TBC). Glasgow 2026/27 for comparison: Arts and Social Sciences GBP 27,720; Science and Engineering GBP 33,210; Medicine MBChB GBP 62,730; Dentistry BDS GBP 58,500. Across the sector a realistic 2026/27 planning range for an IB student from Denmark paying international fees is roughly GBP 22,000-40,000 (about €25,600-46,500) a year for a normal degree, and GBP 45,000-70,000 (about €52,300-81,400) a year for clinical medicine, at the ECB rate of 24 September 2026.

costs.applicationFee: UCAS application fee: GBP 34.50 for up to five choices in the 2027 cycle (GBP 28.95 for 2026 entry).

livingCostMonthly.value: University of Edinburgh estimates GBP 1,546 per month for a single undergraduate living in Edinburgh. London is higher; the Home Office assumes GBP 1,529 per month in London and GBP 1,171 outside London for visa purposes.

notes: For contrast, a UK 'Home' student in England pays a capped fee of GBP 9,790 in 2026-27 and GBP 10,050 in 2027-28. You will not get that rate.
Scottish universities charge EU students the international rate; the pre-Brexit free-tuition arrangement in Scotland ended in 2021.
Visa costs on top of tuition: Student visa GBP 558 from outside the UK, plus the Immigration Health Surcharge at GBP 776 per year of your course (both as published on GOV.UK, September 2026).
Glasgow's 2027/28 medicine and dentistry fees were still marked TBC on 2026-09-24 - re-check before you commit to a clinical course.

funding: UK tuition fee loans and maintenance loans are not available to you as an EU citizen without settled or pre-settled status. Assume you are paying every year in full.

University-run international scholarships are the main realistic source. Almost every university runs merit awards for international undergraduates, usually a partial fee discount of a few thousand pounds; amounts and deadlines are set per university, so check each one.

funding.note: The UK is outside the EU/EEA, so a full degree there follows separate rules, with its own ties-to-Denmark form: check su.dk early.

funding: Some universities still run specific EU-transition or country scholarships; check each course page rather than assuming.
workRights: On a Student visa for a full-time degree at a university, you can work up to 20 hours a week in term time and full time in the holidays (Immigration Rules, Appendix Student, ST 26.1). Your exact limit is printed on your visa.
residency: You need a Student visa. EU citizenship gives you no shortcut since Brexit. You can apply from outside the UK up to 6 months before your course starts; the fee is GBP 558 and you also pay the Immigration Health Surcharge of GBP 776 for each year of your course. You need a Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS) from your university and you must show money for living costs: GBP 1,529 per month for up to 9 months in London, or GBP 1,171 per month outside London, held in your account for 28 consecutive days ending no more than 31 days before you apply. At degree level you can normally stay up to 5 years.
housing: Almost all UK universities guarantee a place in university accommodation to first-year international students who apply by the stated deadline, which is usually in the summer once you have firmly accepted an offer. This is much easier than the Netherlands or Denmark. Apply the moment your firm choice is confirmed.
healthcare: You pay the Immigration Health Surcharge of GBP 776 (about €900) per year as part of the visa application. That gives you access to the NHS on the same basis as a UK resident for the length of your visa. Register with a local GP when you arrive. An EHIC or the Danish yellow card does not replace this.

institutions.name: University of Oxford
institutions.englishBachelors: All courses in English; roughly 50 undergraduate courses
institutions.note: Collegiate, tutorial-based and very narrow: you apply for one subject and study almost only that. The 15 October deadline and an admissions test apply.

institutions.name: University of Cambridge
institutions.englishBachelors: All courses in English; around 30 subject 'Triposes'
institutions.note: Like Oxford, collegiate and supervision-based; entry requirements differ between Colleges and most applicants are interviewed in December.

institutions.name: Imperial College London
institutions.englishBachelors: All courses in English; science, engineering, medicine and business only
institutions.note: Science and engineering only, and unapologetically quantitative - expect HL Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches to be required.

institutions.name: University College London
institutions.englishBachelors: All courses in English; around 400 undergraduate programmes
institutions.note: The broadest subject range of any London university, and one of the few places offering genuinely unusual combinations.

institutions.name: London School of Economics and Political Science
institutions.englishBachelors: All courses in English; social sciences only
institutions.note: Social sciences only and one of the most competitive places in Europe for economics; published IB range is 37 (6,6,6) to 39 (7,6,6).

institutions.name: King's College London
institutions.englishBachelors: All courses in English; broad range across humanities, sciences and health
institutions.note: Strong in health and in war studies/international relations, and a realistic alternative to LSE or UCL in central London.

institutions.name: University of Edinburgh
institutions.englishBachelors: All courses in English; very broad range
institutions.note: Four-year Scottish degrees with flexible early years, in a city many Scandinavian students find easy to settle in; Edinburgh estimates GBP 1,546 a month to live there.

institutions.name: University of Glasgow
institutions.englishBachelors: All courses in English; very broad range
institutions.note: Publishes its IB requirements clearly - Economics asks '36 (6,6,5)' with HL Mathematics (Analysis & Approaches) - and its 2027/28 international fees are already out.
institutions.ibPageNote: Checked 2026-09-23. Glasgow has withdrawn its IB page. The URL previously recorded here — gla.ac.uk/undergraduate/entryrequirements/internationalbaccalaureate/ — redirects to the general entry-requirements page, which says in as many words that "The IB Requirements for each subject can be found on that subject page in the degree programme A-Z". The requirement is therefore per degree, and there is no single page to cite.

institutions.name: University of St Andrews
institutions.englishBachelors: All courses in English; around 200 degree combinations
institutions.note: Not Russell Group but consistently top-ranked, very international, and tiny - a small coastal town, which suits some people and not others.

institutions.name: Durham University
institutions.englishBachelors: All courses in English
institutions.note: Collegiate like Oxbridge and a common second choice for the same applicants; uses the LNAT for law with a 13 January 2027 deadline.

institutions.name: University of Manchester
institutions.englishBachelors: All courses in English; one of the largest UK course catalogues
institutions.note: Very large, very international, and in a city with a much lower cost of living than London.

institutions.name: University of Warwick
institutions.englishBachelors: All courses in English
institutions.note: A campus university with a formidable maths and economics reputation; expect HL Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches for the quantitative courses.

institutions.name: University of Bristol
institutions.englishBachelors: All courses in English
institutions.note: Strong across engineering and the sciences; uses the LNAT for law with an earlier 13 January 2027 test deadline than most.

institutions.name: University of Bath
institutions.englishBachelors: All courses in English
institutions.note: Not Russell Group, but its placement-year degrees and graduate employment record make it a genuinely strong non-Oxbridge option.

institutions.name: Loughborough University
institutions.englishBachelors: All courses in English
institutions.note: Non-Russell Group and the obvious choice if you want sport science or industrial design; offers are usually a few points lower than the Russell Group equivalents.

institutions.name: Lancaster University
institutions.englishBachelors: All courses in English
institutions.note: Collegiate, non-Russell Group, and a realistic target if your predicted points sit in the low 30s.

institutions.name: Queen Mary University of London
institutions.englishBachelors: All courses in English; a broad range including medicine and dentistry
institutions.note: A large Russell Group university in east London, with law, medicine and dentistry among its strengths.

institutions.name: University of Birmingham
institutions.englishBachelors: All courses in English; one of the largest UK course catalogues
institutions.note: A large Russell Group campus university with a very wide subject range, in a city cheaper to live in than London.

institutions.name: University of Leeds
institutions.englishBachelors: All courses in English; one of the largest UK course catalogues
institutions.note: One of the biggest Russell Group universities, with its campus next to the city centre.

institutions.name: City St George's, University of London
institutions.englishBachelors: All courses in English
institutions.note: Formed in 2024 when City, University of London merged with St George's medical school. Business, law and journalism are in Clerkenwell; health and medicine in Tooting.

institutions.name: University of Nottingham
institutions.englishBachelors: All courses in English; very broad range
institutions.note: A Russell Group university on a large parkland campus, with a very broad range of courses.

institutions.name: University of the Arts London
institutions.englishBachelors: All courses in English; art, design, fashion, media and performance
institutions.note: Six colleges, including Central Saint Martins and London College of Fashion. For most courses your portfolio matters more than your IB points.
